status_summary: The National Park Service published a proposed rule on 2026-03-10 (91 FR 11483) that would restore its pre-2015 regulations on hunting, fishing and trapping in Alaska national preserves and rescind, in whole or in part, its 2015, 2017 and 2024 rules. It would remove the bear-baiting prohibition and defer to State rules; the agency estimates no more than 10 bears a year would be taken over bait. Comments were due 2026-04-09 and the deadline was extended to 2026-04-24; the notice page showed 53,801 comments received. A Federal Register search of National Park Service documents through 2026-10-05 returned no final rule. The Fish and Wildlife Service has no matching action: the proposal states that Congress nullified the agency's 2016 refuge rule in 2017 under the Congressional Review Act (Public Law 115-20), and no new refuge rule or state memorandum of understanding was found. The route differs from the Mandate, which pointed to the Congressional Review Act; the National Park Service proposal uses ordinary rulemaking and says its repeal is consistent with, but not required by, the 2017 law.

timeline.event: The National Park Service proposes to restore pre-2015 hunting and trapping rules in Alaska national preserves and rescind its 2015, 2017 and 2024 rules, including the bear-baiting prohibition (91 FR 11483; comments due 2026-04-09).
The National Park Service extends the comment period on the proposal by 15 days, to 2026-04-24, after multiple requests for more time.
